Let's say you go to a casino with $100 and play a game with a 5% house edge (95% expected return value). You may be thinking to yourself "Well, that means I should expect to lose $5 tonight".

The issue is that the % house edge isn't based upon how much you bring to the casino, but rather your total amount wagered. If you play all night you'll win some, lose some, and the whole time the amount wagered will go up. If you wager a total of $1000 in this game, expect to lose 5% of that (in this case, $50). If you wager a total of $2000, expect to lose 5% of that (in this case, you'd lose $100 and be left with nothing. If at this point you have even just $1 left, you're lucky as you should have expected to lose more.

This is why gambling is so profitable - People wager far more than they bring into a casino, unless they lose every single time (which does happen).
